subject.title: `openclaw update` misidentifies pnpm 11 global installations as npm

question: Should the current PR remain a scoped pnpm 11 ownership fix, or must it also replace the shared CLI's shipped npm fallback with an explicit unknown result?
rationale: The pnpm 11 detector change is bounded and directly evidenced, while changing the fallback widens the contract for git, package, and unknown-install callers and needs deliberate upgrade behavior.

options.title: Land detection, track fallback
options.body: Review and land the bounded pnpm 11 ownership fix, then handle explicit unknown-mode behavior as a separately specified compatibility change with caller coverage.

options.title: Expand this fix
options.body: Require this PR to add an unknown-manager contract and update every caller with fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve npm fallback
options.body: Treat npm as the permanent default when ownership is unresolved and close only after pnpm 11 detection lands.

recommendation.title: Land detection, track fallback
recommendation.body: Review and land the bounded pnpm 11 ownership fix, then handle explicit unknown-mode behavior as a separately specified compatibility change with caller coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged updater work most directly owns active package-root detection and package-manager target preservation.
